items.actually_about: Women musicians generically ('Can she play?'), then Clora Bryant

items.actually_about: Hank Jones's own recording output and a Japanese fan
items.notes: Jones does not recall the Milt Jackson date and never addresses Liston.

items.summary: Fuller called his relationship with Liston in Quincy Jones's band a beautiful one and recalled seeing her sit on the bandstand and cry.
items.pull_quote: Oh yeah, that was a beautiful relationship. I've seen her sit on the bandstand and cry.
items.notes: 'her' precedes the Patty Bowen mention and follows a question naming Liston; next block confirms the band is Quincy Jones's and names Melba. Why she cried is not explained -- use with care. 'had to women and it' is a garble of 'had two women in it'.

items.summary: Hampton said he first worked with Liston in Dizzy Gillespie's band and quickly learned how musically heavy she was.
items.pull_quote: I didn’t know that she was as heavy musically as she was. I got in that band. I learned it real fast. Musically, she was heavy.
items.notes: Direct answer to 'is that your first relationship with Melba Liston?' in Gillespie's band.

items.actually_about: Younger women musicians (Ellen Seeling, Diva) inspired by Quincy Jones's band -- Liston and Patti Bown jointly
items.notes: Interviewer paraphrase of legacy influence; immediately preceded by 'And Patti's tunes', so not specific to Liston. Arguably a shared legacy-influence item; reviewer may reconsider.

items.summary: Fuller said he loved every moment of working with Liston and that when he first met her he did not know Gerald Wilson was her husband.
items.pull_quote: Oh, I loved every moment of it
items.notes: Fuller's claim that Gerald Wilson was Liston's husband is his statement only; verify before presenting as fact (standard biographies describe Wilson as a bandleader/mentor she worked for).
Joe Williams's roommate story moves to the hotel; Liston only in the anchor.

items.actually_about: Min Xiao Fen (pipa player) and the Khepera project
items.notes: 'she' = Min Xiao Fen. The next (context) block says Melba did the Khepera arrangements, but this block does not mention her.

items.actually_about: Mary Lou Williams herself (Dizzy getting her to Newport, priests, fasting)
items.notes: Opens with the tail of Liston's quoted line from the anchor ('...I just sat / down and took the music down.'). Any Liston quote should be built from the anchor plus that first clause, not from this block.

items.notes: 'Henson' in the prior question is a garble of Jensen.

items.summary: Powell said Liston had moved to New York two or three years earlier, had been wheelchair-bound for a while, and was very close to Randy Weston.
items.pull_quote: She’s been here for about two or three years. She’s been wheelchair bound for a little while, but she and Randy are very close
items.notes: First half about Liston; block then pivots to Randy Weston's kindness and Powell's dialysis. Ends with a page footer artefact.

items.summary: Higginbotham praised Liston's trombone playing and recalled her grabbing him at a Sunday afternoon session.
items.notes: Interviewer interjected a question about Sweets Edison just before; 'trombone' and 'She' indicate Higginbotham is still on Liston, but '(That boy)' is an uncertain transcription. Anchor misnames her 'Melvin Liston'. Text is fragmentary.
